name: Bitly
tagline: Short links, branded back-halves, QR codes, and click analytics

pricing.notes: Growth listed because it is the cheapest tier that includes a custom domain, which is the whole point of paying · Core at 10 USD/month is annual-billed only and gives you no branded links at all. Growth is 35 USD billed monthly or 29 USD billed annually. Free is 5 links/month with no data history. Premium is 199 USD/month annual-billed.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 5 links/month; 2 QR codes/month; 2 landing pages; 3 custom back-halves/month; 1,000 API requests/month; unlimited clicks/scans

tiers.name: Core
tiers.limits: 100 links/month; 5 QR codes/month; 5 landing pages; 5 redirects/month; 5,000 API requests/month; 30-day analytics history

tiers.name: Growth
tiers.limits: 500 links/month; 10 QR codes/month; 10 landing pages; 20 redirects/month; 25,000 API requests/month; 120-day history; 1 custom domain

tiers.name: Premium
tiers.limits: 3,000 links/month; 200 QR codes/month; 20 landing pages; 110 redirects/month; 50,000 API requests/month; 1-year history

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom links, QR codes, landing pages, API volume and users; 2-year analytics history

pricing.freeTierCaps: 5 links/month, 2 QR codes/month, 2 landing pages, 3 custom back-halves/month, 1,000 API requests/month, and unlimited clicks/scans
pricing.billingTerms: Core annual only; Growth and Premium monthly + annual; plans auto-renew and sales tax may apply
pricing.hiddenCosts: Core cannot be bought monthly. Feature quotas reset monthly; extra enterprise capabilities such as parameter passing can be separately purchasable, and sales tax may be added.

verdictSummary: A slug, a lookup, a 302, and a row in a table. Cloudflare Workers plus KV and D1 does the whole job on the free tier, and QR codes are one library call. The only thing you are really buying is that bit.ly resolves links created in 2012 and will presumably still resolve them in 2032, which is an institutional promise rather than a technical one. If the links are going in a magazine ad or on packaging, that promise is worth something. If they are going in this week's newsletter, it is worth nothing, and Growth is 420 USD a year.
coreLoopDIY: Map a short slug to a destination, 302 to it, log the click with device and country, and render a QR code for any link.
whatYouLose: links that outlive your own infrastructure · a domain you stop renewing takes every link with it
bit.ly's recognition in the link itself, which cuts both ways now that shorteners get spam-filtered
bundled QR code management, landing pages, and campaign grouping
city-level and device-level analytics rollups without building them
an SLA and someone to call
whyPeopleStillPay: Bitly's actual product is a promise about the future: that a link printed on a box in 2019 still resolves today. No amount of code buys that, only an institution that intends to keep existing. Teams also pay for shared workspaces, SSO, and the audit trail, and marketing departments pay because the alternative is asking engineering for a redirect and waiting two weeks.

alternatives.name: Dub
alternatives.desc: Bitly with deeper attribution; self-hosting means recreating half a startup's infrastructure.

facts.install: Hosted signup, or a source deployment assembled across Vercel, MySQL/PlanetScale, Tinybird, Upstash and Cloudflare R2/AWS
facts.dataFormat: Dub Cloud stores links, users and analytics in Dub's infrastructure; the documented self-hosted stack keeps link/user metadata in PlanetScale-compatible MySQL, click events in Tinybird/ClickHouse, redirect cache and jobs in Upstash Redis/QStash, and assets in Cloudflare R2 or AWS.
facts.gapVsPaid: Dub has richer attribution, but self-hosting depends on several external databases, queues, analytics, storage, email, and deployment services and still lacks Bitly's enterprise support and governance.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting is not one Compose file: the official guide requires accounts, credentials and configuration across GitHub, Tinybird, Upstash, MySQL/PlanetScale, Vercel and Cloudflare or AWS.

alternatives.name: Shlink
alternatives.desc: Branded links, routing rules and serious click stats in one container; the QR endpoint is living on borrowed time.

facts.install: Run the official Docker image, or unpack the PHP distribution and connect SQLite, MySQL/MariaDB, PostgreSQL or SQL Server
facts.dataFormat: Short links, domains, tags, visits and geolocation records live in the configured relational database; cache files live in Shlink's writable `data` directory, and the separate web client talks to the server through an API key.
facts.gapVsPaid: Shlink supplies the shortening API and analytics, but the user must host a separate web client, operate the server, and accept that its built-in QR endpoint is being deprecated.
facts.setupBlocker: The first hurdle is operating two pieces, a Shlink API plus its web client, and supplying a public domain, HTTPS, database persistence and an API key; built-in QR generation is deprecated.

alternatives.name: Short.io
alternatives.desc: A thousand branded links, QR codes and real analytics before the pricing page becomes relevant.

facts.install: Hosted signup, then connect a custom domain
facts.engines: Optional Short.io AI allowance; the underlying model provider is not disclosed
facts.dataFormat: Links, custom-domain configuration, QR assets and click/conversion analytics live in Short.io's cloud; links can be exported through support, but the internal storage format is not disclosed.
facts.gapVsPaid: Short.io's free plan is generous, but the lifetime link ceiling and smaller campaign, governance, integration, and enterprise-support surface make it less durable than paid Bitly.
facts.setupBlocker: There is no installation hurdle, but the free account has a lifetime ceiling of 1,000 branded links, one user, 10 MB storage and only the first 50,000 clicks per month visible in analytics.

alternatives.name: Sink
alternatives.desc: A polished Bitly clone on Cloudflare; free hosting, several bindings, and no server to patch.

facts.install: Fork the repository and deploy a Cloudflare Worker with D1 and KV bindings; Analytics Engine, R2 and Workers AI are optional
facts.engines: Optional Cloudflare Workers AI for slug and OpenGraph suggestions
facts.dataFormat: The user's Cloudflare account holds links in D1, redirect cache in Workers KV, visit events in Analytics Engine and optional JSON snapshots or social images in R2; the public demo uses the maintainer's Cloudflare account.
facts.gapVsPaid: Sink is elegant on Cloudflare, but it lacks Bitly's mature QR campaign management, team permissions, branded-link governance, integrations, and vendor support.
facts.setupBlocker: A non-expert must create and wire several Cloudflare resources, copy binding IDs, set a stable site token and understand build-time versus runtime secrets.

notes: You are not paying for the redirect · you are paying for the promise that it still works in ten years.
prompt:
Build me a link shortener with click analytics and QR codes to replace Bitly. Requirements:

- Cloudflare Workers via wrangler: KV for the slug lookup, D1 for the click
  log. Free tier, and it runs on my own domain.
- A worker on go.mydomain.com/{slug} reads KV and 302s, writing the click to
  D1 inside ctx.waitUntil so the redirect never waits on the database.
- Slugs are random 6-character base62 by default, but I can set a custom
  back-half, and creating one that already exists fails loudly instead of
  overwriting it.
- Log per click: slug, timestamp, country and city from request.cf,
  device type parsed from the user-agent, and referer.
- Generate a PNG QR code for any link with the qrcode npm package, served at
  /qr/{slug} and cached, so print material points at the same tracked link.
- Optional expiry and a click cap per link · past either, 302 to a fallback
  URL I set instead of returning a 404.
- An /admin page behind one password (wrangler secret) listing links with
  clicks per day, plus top countries and device split per link.
- Secrets via wrangler secret, never in wrangler.toml. No accounts, no
  third-party analytics, no telemetry.
- README: wrangler setup, the KV namespace and D1 database, the DNS record,
  and a warning that these links die with the domain, so use a domain you
  intend to keep renewing.
